title: Each check-in, membership look and receipt save reads every membership or payment the gym ever had
what: To find one member's plans, the server goes through all of the gym's memberships, and to work out what a membership still owes on each receipt save it goes through all of the gym's payments. There is no index on which member or which membership a row belongs to, so the work grows with every year of the gym's history. The QR check-in, the member's My membership screen, the gym's workout plans in the app, the branch visitor check and every receipt save all do this. Crispy Curves has 1 membership and 1 payment today, so nobody feels it yet; a 500-member gym after a few years holds thousands of each.
expected: Looking up one member's plans or one membership's payments touches only those rows, however old the gym is.
who: members checking in, owners and desk saving receipts at big old gyms
how_often: every check-in, receipt save and membership screen open
fix_line: Add an index on the member and on the membership inside the gym's memberships and payments.

title: Deleting a gym reads the offer history and the photo-upload passes of every gym
what: The workout-offer history and the short-lived photo-upload passes are linked to their gym, but that link has no index. When HQ deletes a gym, the database has to read these lists for all gyms to find the rows to remove. Both lists are small today, so the cost is tiny; the offer history grows with every offer at every gym.
expected: Every link from a list to its gym has an index, so deleting one gym touches only its own rows.
how_often: each time a gym is deleted
fix_line: Add an index on the gym column of the offer history and the photo-upload passes.
